subject.title: fix(clickclack): deliver media and configurable model replies [AI-assisted]

question: Should this PR ship the new per-account maxTokens surface and change unset ClickClack model replies from the shipped 96-token cap to runtime/model defaults, or should that policy be reviewed separately from media delivery?
rationale: The runtime-default behavior fixes demonstrated message loss, but it also changes the cost and latency profile of every existing model-mode account and introduces a new public configuration surface.

options.title: Split the policy change
options.body: Land media delivery separately and review maxTokens plus the unset-default behavior in a focused follow-up with explicit upgrade and cost acceptance.

options.title: Approve the combined behavior
options.body: Accept runtime/model defaults when unset and the optional 1–32768 account override as the intended ClickClack product contract.

options.title: Retain a bounded default
options.body: Choose and document a non-96 fixed default, then prove it across representative reasoning and non-reasoning models before merge.

recommendation.title: Split the policy change
recommendation.body: Land media delivery separately and review maxTokens plus the unset-default behavior in a focused follow-up with explicit upgrade and cost acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available recent contributor on the ClickClack client boundary affected by both delivery semantics and compatibility validation.
